name: DEA Drug Slang - Depressants & Benzodiazepines
description: Slang terms and code words the DEA associates with depressants & benzodiazepines, from its own 2018 reference for law enforcement. Matched as whole words.

source.title: DEA Intelligence Report DEA-HOU-DIR-022-18, 'Slang Terms and Code Words: A Reference for Law Enforcement Personnel'
source.licence: Public domain - a work of the United States Government, 17 U.S.C. 105. Marked UNCLASSIFIED in the original.

caveats: This is a July 2018 snapshot. Drug slang moves quickly, and terms for substances that became common after 2018 will not be here.

Many entries are ordinary English words used as slang (Ice, Boy, Pot, Work, Bars). Each term is matched as a whole word, but no pattern can tell the slang sense from the innocent one - expect false positives and prune the list to your case.
A hit is a lead, not a finding. The DEA compiled these from law-enforcement and open sources; presence of a word is not evidence of an offence.
